candidates.title: GAINet: Dual Difference-Perception Geometry and Appearance Interactive Network for Light Field Occlusion Removal
candidates.abstract: Light field (LF) captures rich spatial-angular information, enabling effective occlusion removal. Existing LF methods rely on appearance cues (e.g., texture and color) to reconstruct the appearance of input. However, without explicit modeling of spatial relationships and geometric (e.g., depth) constraints, appearance-driven methods suffer from structural distortion, residual occlusions, and blurriness.In this paper, we propose a novel dual difference-perception geometry-appearance interactive network (GAINet) for LF de-occlusion. GAINet integrates geometry de-occlusion and appearance de-occlusion by a dual difference-perception interaction network and achieves mutual promotion of their performance. Specifically, the geometry reconstructor restores occlusion-free depth to explicitly model the spatial-geometric relationships, reconstructing reasonable structure. Guided by this occlusion-free depth, the appearance reconstructor utilizes rich spatial-angular cues for accurate occlusion-free reconstruction. To realize mutual promotion, appearance-difference perception highlights regions with suboptimal reconstruction and guides the geometry reconstructor to prioritize geometric refinement in non-ideal regions of the de-occlusion. Conversely, geometry-difference perception propagates depth errors back to the appearance reconstructor, enabling focused improvement in appearance fidelity.Then, an edge-region enhancement module is introduced to alleviate over-smoothing and artifacts caused by unreliable occlusion masks. Moreover, to mitigate redundancy and blurriness during multi-view fusion, we propose an adaptive view fusion attention that adaptively focuses on informative views to ensure high-fidelity reconstruction. Experiments demonstrate that GAINet achieves superior qualitative and quantitative performance compared with state-of-the-art methods. On public synthetic datasets, GAINet attains the best average results of 34.50 dB PSNR and 0.956 SSIM, achieving performance gains of 16.0\% and 5.8\%, respectively.

candidates.title: Light-field-aware physics-informed learning for super-resolved volumetric flow reconstruction from sparse light field particle image velocimetry measurements
candidates.abstract: Light field particle image velocimetry (LF-PIV) enables single-camera volumetric flow measurement, but its performance is limited by low spatial resolution and large depth-wise velocity uncertainty. This study proposes a LF-aware physics-informed neural network (LF-PINN) for super-resolved flow reconstructions from sparse LF-PIV measurements. Building on standard PINNs, which enforce governing equations during learning, the proposed method further incorporates LF imaging characteristics into the physics-informed framework to improve the reconstruction accuracy. This is achieved by introducing a degradation model and a reliability-weighted learning strategy that account for the spatial averaging effect and the anisotropic velocity uncertainty inherent in LF-PIV measurements. Numerical tests on forced isotropic turbulence demonstrate that LF-PINN effectively corrects depth-wise velocity errors, reducing the relative error of the depth-wise velocity component to below 10% when initial measurement errors reach 20%. Incorporating pressure information further enhances flow reconstruction accuracy, reducing the root mean square divergence of the flow field by 22%. Compared with standard PINN formulations and a proper orthogonal decomposition-based interpolation method, LF-PINN achieves superior performance in both spatial and temporal super-resolution reconstruction from sparse measurements. Fine-scale vortical structures and turbulence statistics are recovered with higher fidelity. Experimental measurements of the wake behind a circular cylinder further show that LF-PINN produces clearer wake structures and velocity profiles that are in better consistence with planar-PIV references. These results demonstrate that embedding LF imaging characteristics into physics-informed learning provides an effective route toward super-resolved and physically consistent volumetric flow reconstruction.

candidates.title: Blind Light Field Image Quality Assessment via Cross-View Encoding and Dynamic Expert Mixture
Vector light-field distribution in non-line-of-sight ultraviolet wireless communication
candidates.abstract: Extensive studies on non-line-of-sight ultraviolet (NLOS UV) communications have primarily focused on path loss or channel impulse response. By leveraging Monte Carlo-based methods that can track photon trajectories and capture angular information of received photons, this paper further investigates the directional distribution characteristics of the arriving light at the receiver. To this end, we first establish a three-dimensional vector light-field distribution model for arbitrary sampling points in space based on Monte Carlo photon trajectory tracking. Then, by constructing the response distribution over discrete detection directions, we extract the dominant receiving direction and its corresponding angle, which characterize the principal arrival orientation of photon energy. Based on the proposed model, the effects of transmitter elevation angle, spatial position, and related parameters on the directional response distribution and the dominant receiving direction are analyzed. Experiments are conducted in representative scenarios under both coplanar and non-coplanar conditions. The experimental results agree well with the theoretical analysis, demonstrating that the proposed method can effectively characterize the directional properties of NLOS UV channels. The obtained results provide useful insights for future studies on receiver orientation optimization, direction selection, and spatial/angular diversity reception design.

candidates.title: Dynamic Light Fields Empowering the Microcosmos: Advances in Optoelectronic Tweezers
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Optoelectronic tweezers (OET) is a micro/nano‐manipulation technology based on light‐induced dielectrophoresis, offering noncontact operation, dynamic reconfigurability, low photodamage, and good biocompatibility. Owing to these advantages, OET has emerged as an important manipulation platform in microscale science. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in OET from five perspectives: fundamental mechanisms, device implementation, performance regulation, cross‐scale applications, and intelligent integration. First, the working principles of OET are introduced, together with representative chip architectures, optical implementation strategies, and the application scenarios of existing photoconductive materials. The key factors governing manipulation performance‐including electrical parameters, light‐pattern characteristics, medium properties, and target‐object attributes‐are then analyzed. On this basis, the applications of OET in nanomaterial assembly, microparticle manipulation, single‐cell sorting, information readout, and microenvironment construction are reviewed. Furthermore, integrated and automated systems enabled by the combination of OET with microfluidics, droplet manipulation, and intelligent algorithms are discussed, highlighting their potential for high‐throughput operation and clinical translation. Overall, OET is evolving from a single‐function manipulation tool into a platform technology featuring multi‐module coordination, system‐level integration, and intelligent operation. This review is expected to provide a systematic reference for the mechanistic understanding, device design, application expansion, and system‐level optimization of OET.

candidates.title: Analysis of light field refocusing methods for sparse input views
candidates.abstract: Light field imaging technology enables digital refocusing with “shoot first, focus later” capability, but acquiring its high-dimensional data involves an inherent trade-off between spatial and angular resolution. To address the challenge of refocusing under sparse angular sampling, we present a comparative analysis of two representative technical approaches: end-to-end methods based on deep learning and multi-stage methods based on traditional image processing. Experimental results on the Stanford Light Field Dataset demonstrate that RefocusNet, with its end-to-end architecture, achieves inference speeds in milliseconds, making it well-suited for resource-constrained scenes. In contrast, methods based on bokeh rendering (BR) and super-resolution deliver superior refocusing quality and support post-capture adjustment of the depth of field, making them more appropriate for practical applications. We provide a reference framework for selecting sparse light field refocusing algorithms for different applications.

candidates.title: Quaternary-squeeze quantum identity authentication: Direction-scaling security via single-mode squeezed light
candidates.abstract: Quantum identity authentication (QIA) has emerged as a crucial technology for secure communication systems, particularly in the burgeoning era of quantum communications. This paper proposes a novel QIA protocol based on non-classical characteristics of squeezed light fields. By exploiting the quantum noise reduction properties of quadrature squeezed coherent states, the protocol fundamentally thwarts eavesdropping attempts by Heisenberg-limited uncertainty constraints. The fidelity parameter for decoy states is utilized to detect spoofing attacks, and the dynamic key update mechanism fundamentally eliminates vulnerabilities caused by key reuse. Security information ratio analysis shows that the protocol is able to resist Gaussian-cloner attacks and detect eavesdropping. Moreover, the security threshold can be further enhanced with higher squeezing, allowing tunable protection levels adaptable to different threat scenarios. Compared with binary-squeezed protocols, our proposed four-direction (quaternary-dimensional) squeezing halves the eavesdropper's guessing probability and enlarges the fidelity gap by 29%, tightening the discrimination threshold without relying on extra hardware, thus facilitating practical implementation.

candidates.title: Physics-Conditioned FiLM-UNet for Fast Volumetric Light-Field Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: We present a physics-conditioned, self-supervised deep learning network for Fourier light-field microscopy reconstruction, achieving robust performance across varying experimental conditions and outperforming conventional networks trained with a single PSF in accuracy and generalization.

candidates.title: Kilohertz In Vivo Neural Voltage Imaging with Light Field Microscopy via Physics Guided LISTA-Net Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: We demonstrate 1 kHz in-vivo neuronal voltage imaging using light field microscopy. A physics-inspired deep network reconstructs artifact-suppressed volumes. Then, one high-contrast reference volume is forward-projected into light-field ROIs for fast extraction of neural activity.

candidates.title: Scanning wide-field tomography for functional imaging of freely-swimming larval zebrafish in vivo
candidates.abstract: High-speed functional imaging of biological samples, such as larval zebrafish, at cellular resolutions in freely moving states is indispensable in the study of neuronal basis of naturalistic behaviors. However, current strategy of mechanically moving samples to keep them within the field-of-view is not only slow but also susceptible to disturb the free states of the samples. Here, we propose the scanning wide-field tomography (SWIFT), based on Fourier light field microscopy and random-access scanning, and achieve ~4.6×4.6×0.32 mm 3 volume-of-view (VoV) at micrometre resolutions. By taking advantages of SWIFT in large VoV and flexible imaging, we successfully demonstrate functional imaging of freely-swimming larval zebrafish in vivo , while keeping zebrafish in truly natural states though remote tracking.

candidates.title: FCPA-Net: Fourier Channel Prior Attention Network for Blind Light Field Image Quality Assessment
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

candidates.title: DD-SOD: Dual-Depth Supervised Learning for Light Field Salient Object Detection
candidates.abstract: Weakly supervised light field salient object detection (LFSOD) still faces many challenges. Existing methods consistently use the original light-field depth map as a fixed input, capping performance at its inherent quality, while also fail to fully utilize the implicit depth information contained in the focal-stacks, which requires complex feature extraction. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dual-Depth supervised learning for Light Field Salient Object Detection, DD-SOD, which for the first time introduces a depth estimation mechanism jointly supervised by Dual-Depth cues—the light field depth map and the monocular depth map from the Depth Anything model. This allows the model to mine the depth information of the focal-stacks and autonomously learn depth cues, rather than relying on a fixed input, thereby promoting the synergistic optimization of depth cue quality and feature fusion performance. Simultaneously, we design an Adaptive Feature Fusion module that mitigates the inconsistency caused by heterogeneous representations between the depth cues and the all-in-focus through dynamic feature reweighting, achieving robust fusion. Extensive experiments on three popular LFSOD benchmark datasets demonstrate that DD-SOD achieves state-of-theart performance, especially in complex backgrounds and weakly textured scenes, validating the effectiveness and originality of the proposed depth estimation mechanism.

candidates.title: Review of light-driven soft robotics: Materials, fabrication, modulation and applications
candidates.abstract: Compared with conventional rigid robots, soft robots offer superior environmental adaptability and safer human–robot interaction. Light-driven soft robots have attracted increasing attention because of their remote controllability, non-contact actuation, and miniaturization potential. This review systematically classifies light-responsive materials according to their response mechanisms and summarizes their actuation characteristics. Recent advances in fabrication technologies and light-field regulation strategies are also reviewed to provide an integrated perspective on the design and control of light-driven soft robots. Representative applications, including biomimetic locomotion and biomedical systems, are discussed. Finally, current challenges and future opportunities are highlighted, focusing on advanced light-responsive materials, biosafety and clinical translation, and multifunctional system integration. This review provides an updated reference for the development of next-generation light-driven soft robots.
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part L: Journal of Materials: Design and Applications

candidates.title: Internal Cooling Tube Geometry with Integrated Leds Affects Light Distribution and Chlorella Vulgaris Growth
candidates.abstract:
Background: Temperature control remains a bottleneck in bench-scale photobioreactor (PBR) operation. Internal cooling tubes improve heat removal but inevitably obstruct light. Winding LED strips directly around cooling tubes-co-locating the light source and heat exchangermay mitigate this trade-off, but the effect of tube geometry on the resulting light field has not been experimentally quantified. 

Methods: Three internal cooling-tube geometries (serpentine coil, vertical straight tube, horizontal straight tube), each fabricated from identical borosilicate glass (OD 8 mm, length 900 mm) and fitted with identical flexible LED strips (660 + 450 nm), were compared against a notube control in 1.5-L batch cultures of Chlorella vulgaris (n = 3 per treatment, 12 beakers total). Spatial PAR distribution (5 × 5 grid, 25 positions per beaker), temperature at three depths, biomass (OD₇₅₀/CDW), chlorophyll content, and pH were monitored over 12 days. Data were analysed by one-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD post-hoc tests (α = 0.05) using R 4.3.1. 

Results: The serpentine coil provided the most uniform temperature control (intra-beaker spatial range 0.5 ± 0.2 °C vs. 1.1 ± 0.3 °C for vertical and 1.6 ± 0.4 °C for horizontal tubes). Net PAR obstruction was 8.2 ± 2.9% (serpentine), 7.5 ± 2.6% (vertical), and 14.1 ± 3.2% (horizontal; P = 0.012 vs. serpentine). Despite these differences, final biomass (1.69-1.82 g L⁻¹) and specific growth rate (0.36-0.43 d⁻¹) did not differ significantly among the cooled configurations (P = 0.18-0.52), consistent with operation above the light-saturation threshold of C. vulgaris. 

Conclusions: Under the tested conditions (~120 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹), tube geometry measurably affects light distribution and temperature uniformity but not growth. The serpentine coil with integrated LED lighting offers the best combination of thermal performance and apparatus simplicity for bench-scale experiments where temperature-sensitive endpoints are of interest.

candidates.title: Generation of complex structured light by cascading of topological charge and geometric phase
candidates.abstract: Abstract We employ the spin–orbit interaction (SOI) of light within an interferometer that confines light in a closed rectangular path. This configuration enables the cascading of topological charge and geometric phase for the generation of vector and vortex beams. Thus, we introduce a half-wave plate (HWP) and q-plate within the interferometer, so that for an input circularly polarized Gaussian beam, the passage of light through the q-plate leads to the generation of orbital angular momentum (OAM) due to SOI effects. Each successive pass inside the interferometer amplifies the OAM due to the presence of the HWP, so that finally, we generate a series of vortex beams carrying increasing topological charge at the output. A key feature of this configuration is the cascading of topological charge and Pancharatnam–Berry phase, arising from the sequential evolution of the circular polarization state and vortex phase. Furthermore, when the input beam is linearly polarized, the interferometer produces a series of vector beams exhibiting polarization patterns akin to a multipole expansion, which we can quantify theoretically by a Jones vector analysis. Experimentally, we quantified both the vortex and vector beams up to the third order, along with the accumulation of the geometric phase up to the second order at the interferometer output. These effects were observed by deliberately misaligning the interferometer, thereby restricting the beam to three successive circulations within the loop. Our work highlights the utility of an interferometer for generating structured light fields with tunable intensity, polarization, and phase.

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Multiview Cartoon Character Modeling: Physics-Consistent Inverse Rendering for Dynamic-Backlight Light-Field 3D Display
candidates.abstract: Three-dimensional display is fundamentally a problem of reconstructing view-dependent optical rays rather than presenting planar images. Multilayer light field display provides an effective panel-based route for 3D scene reconstruction, but it remains constrained by two coupled bottlenecks: additional attenuation layers can improve angular reconstruction while reducing transmitted light, and higher spatio-angular density increases the cost of inverse synthesis. This study proposes a dynamic-backlight-enabled multilayer framework in which a pixel-addressable emission plane participates in light-field synthesis, thereby replacing one purely passive illumination stage with a controllable optical degree of freedom. The emitted rays of conventional- and dynamic-backlight configurations are represented by a unified non-negative tensor model, and layer synthesis is formulated as a weighted non-negative tensor factorization (NTF) problem. A physics-consistent convolutional neural network is further used to predict display-layer patterns through the same optical forward model and is extended from 5 × 5 to 10 × 10 viewpoint inputs. The quantitative evidence reported in this paper comprises NTF runtime and test-set PSNR, whereas the prototype photographs provide qualitative verification of viewpoint reconstruction. Because the conventional and dynamic prototypes use different LCD and OLED panels that were not luminance- or color-matched, their apparent brightness and contrast differences are not interpreted as calibrated measurements of architectural gain. Within this evidence boundary, the results support proof-of-concept feasibility of jointly designing the emission plane, attenuation layers, and inverse solver, rather than complete validation of a practical electronically addressable multilayer display.

candidates.title: A reconfigurable, broadband light-field mapper for illusionary effects
candidates.abstract: The manipulation of light field is pivotal for advancing optical technologies. Here, we present a reconfigurable optical system based on lens-fiber networks that function as a light-field mapper, capable of generating macroscopic optical illusions. This system employs a lens array to decompose the incident light field, which is then transmitted via a fiber network and reconstructed by a second lens array. This process establishes a reconfigurable mapping between input and output light fields. Through proof-of-principle experiments, we demonstrate “free-space” illusion devices, where light rays traverse the mapper—including embedded opaque objects—in straight lines, effectively mimicking propagation through free space. Our work introduces a flexible platform for light-field manipulation with potential applications in virtual reality, optical computing, and secure communication.

candidates.title: Multifunctional miniature robots: Harnessing the photothermal effect of magnetic microparticles for light and magnetic control
candidates.abstract: Developing miniature robots with multimodal mobility in complex environments remains challenging. This study developed miniature robots based on magnetic particle–doped liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) that integrate multicomponent functional doped materials and LCE molecular orientation engineering. Thanks to the synergistic introduction of magnetic particles with photothermal effects and 5CB plasticizer, the robot exhibits fast photothermal response in both terrestrial and underwater environments. In the terrestrial environment, the designed photomagnetic dual-field coupling strategy reshapes the physical boundaries of robots, improving their obstacle-crossing ability and achieving asymmetric full-orientation dual-mode jumping. In the underwater environment, the robot utilizes frequency laser flapping to induce wake vortex rings to overcome moderate Reynolds number drag. Especially, by utilizing the spatial resolution of the local light field, it successfully achieves efficient directional propulsion and flexible steering control by switching the irradiation position to break fluid symmetry, substantially alleviating the spatial-control limitations of globally applied magnetic fields. Finally, we demonstrated potential applications of designed miniature robots on targeted photothermal therapy of cancer cells with high accuracy. We expect that the newly developed dual-responsive and multifunctional miniature robots will find broad medical applications, such as targeted drug delivery and minimally invasive surgery.

candidates.title: Comparison of radiation and light field congruence between a developed collimator test tool and a standard collimator test tool in the general X-ray units of Lamphun Province hospitals
candidates.abstract: Background: Assessment of radiation and light-field congruence is a key quality-control procedure for general X-ray machines. This process typically requires a standard collimator test tool, which can be costly. Therefore, the author developed an innovative collimator test tool as a cost-effective alternative for evaluating the congruence between the radiation field and the collimator light field. Objectives: The present study aims to evaluate and compare radiation and light-field congruence measured using the developed collimator test tool and a standard tool on general X-ray units across eight hospitals in Lamphun Province. Materials and methods: The developed collimator test tool was constructed from an etched stainless-steel plate measuring 20×25 cm, with scale resolutions of 2.5 mm and 5 mm. The standard collimator test tool (GAMMEX, Model 161B) is made from a brass plate of the same dimensions with a scale resolution of 5 mm. Measurements followed the 2023 diagnostic X-ray quality standards established by the Department of Medical Sciences, Ministry of Public Health. Radiation and light field borders were measured three times on each of four sides, yielding a total of 96 measurements. Error and percentage error were calculated, and a paired-sample t-test analysis was performed. Results: Comparison of radiation and light-field congruence between the developed collimator and the standard collimator test tools revealed a maximum error of 0.5 mm, corresponding to a percentage error of 3%, which is below the acceptable limits of 1 mm or 5%. Statistical analysis using a paired-sample t-test (p<0.05) indicated no significant difference between measurements obtained from the two test tools (p≥0.05). Conclusion: The developed collimator test tool can be used as an alternative to the standard tool for radiation and light field congruence testing in general X-ray units. It offers a cost-effective option for self-quality control and monitoring in radiology departments while maintaining the same measurement accuracy.

candidates.title: High-resolution, video-rate light-field displays enabled by a field-sequential-color LCD: all driven by computations
candidates.abstract: Light-field displays (LFDs) fundamentally suffer from low spatial resolution, constrained by the pixel count of available microdisplays. Field-sequential color liquid crystal displays (FSC-LCDs) offer a promising solution by temporally mixing colors without color filters, thereby enabling a threefold increase in resolution. However, deploying FSC-LCDs for LFD applications remains challenging due to panel fabrication hurdles and the computational bottlenecks associated with rendering elemental image arrays (EIAs) and mitigating color breakup (CBU) artifacts at video rates. To overcome these challenges, we first develop a 2.3K-by-2.3 K (1500 ppi) FSC-LCD featuring a high aperture ratio and fast response time. We then propose a unified, video-rate computational framework. This pipeline achieves high efficiency through two key innovations: (i) an EIA module that leverages a pre-computed voxel-pixel look-up table (LUT) to bypass real-time ray tracing, and (ii) an FSC module that utilizes a lightweight neural network to infer optimal backlight signals for CBU suppression and color fidelity. We validated this end-to-end architecture on an LFD prototype. While maintaining accurate focus cues, optical reconstructions yield an angular voxel density of approximately 18 pixels per degree (PPD) across a 59.8° field of view, surpassing contemporary LFDs in total resolution. Finally, a dynamic 3D image acquisition and processing pipeline starting from a commercial depth camera demonstrated the system’s computational efficiency, with the core EIA and FSC modules executing in just 32.7 ms on a CPU-GPU computing platform, establishing a scalable foundation for next-generation extended reality (XR) displays.

candidates.title: 3D Microscale Flow Field Measurement of Light Field Based on Experimental Fitting of PSF Deconvolution Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: Accurate measurement of microscale 3D flow characteristics is a core prerequisite for optimizing microfluidic chips, micro-thrusters and other micro-devices. The emerging light field Micro-PIV technique can capture full light field information of the flow field via a single one-exposure camera, and reconstruct instantaneous 3D positions of tracer particles to realize 3D velocity field measurement. However, the introduced microlens array breaks the translation invariance of the system point spread function (PSF), making direct experimental PSF acquisition impossible. Since 3D flow reconstruction strictly relies on the PSF, the reconstruction quality is highly dependent on PSF accuracy. This work proposes a computational PSF calibration method, which iteratively adjusts the inter-component distance parameters of the light field system by matching the similarity between simulated and experimental PSFs, to obtain a high-precision calibrated PSF. The resolution distribution near the objective focal plane is characterized, and the 3D flow field inside a T-shaped microchannel is measured using the established system and the calibrated PSF.

candidates.title: Snapshot-based method for wide-spectral-range and wide-field broadband-integrated BTDF measurement
candidates.abstract: Snapshot BTDF measurement faces significant challenges in simultaneously achieving an ultra-wide angular range and broad spectral coverage, while generally applicable spatial calibration algorithms are still lacking. To address these issues, this study proposes a snapshot wide-field broadband-integrated BTDF measurement method and the corresponding system architecture. First, a light-field transfer model is established to elucidate the propagation, accommodation, and acquisition mechanisms of off-axis light fields. Second, a wide-field catadioptric imaging optical system is designed. After optimization, the modulation transfer function (MTF) across the entire field of view exceeds 0.35 at the cutoff spatial frequency, while the distortion is maintained below 23%. To compensate for off-axis imaging distortion, a spatial-mapping correction method based on a hybrid-structured radial lattice is proposed. A hybrid mapping strategy is then used to establish correspondence between the lattices and achieve high-accuracy spatial correction. Combined simulations demonstrate that the effective measurable zenith-angle range is substantially extended to 2 ∘ –55 ∘ , with resolvable angular sampling intervals of 1 ∘ and 10 ∘ in the zenith and azimuth directions, respectively, thereby effectively reducing the measurement blind zone at small zenith angles. After correction, the coefficient of variation remains within 0.366–0.452 over the zenith-angle range of 34 ∘ –55 ∘ . Moreover, the maximum relative error in the measurement of a standard Lambertian target is only 1.08%. Accordingly, the primary contribution of this work is the substantial reduction of the measurement blind zone at small zenith angles rather than the pursuit of the largest possible zenith angle. Specifically, the lower bound of the effective measurable zenith-angle range is reduced from the original 20 ∘ to 2 ∘ , enabling snapshot BTDF measurements over the 2 ∘ –55 ∘ range.These simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method and provide a basis for prototype development and experimental validation.

candidates.title: Axially sparse volumetric illumination-based light-field microscopy overcoming reconstruction limitations on z-ambiguity and near-NFP degradation
candidates.abstract: Light-field microscopy (LFM) captures volumetric fluorescence in a single exposure but is constrained by the spatial–angular sampling trade-off of a detector with a limited pixel count, leading to two major reconstruction limitations: z-ambiguity, which results in low and depth-dependent axial resolution, and severe reconstruction degradation near the nominal focal plane (NFP). Here, we present modulated light-sheet light-field microscopy (MoLiS-LFM), which acquires multiple z-sparse light-field images per volume using mutually independent, z-modulated light-sheet excitation. This approach effectively guarantees sparsity in the reconstructed volume and thereby improves axial resolving and localization capabilities. In addition, piezo-driven objective displacement shifts the NFP relative to the stationary specimen for a complementary MoLiS-LFM acquisition, leveraging LFM’s high-fidelity off-focus reconstruction to reduce near-NFP degradation. Fluorescent-bead experiments demonstrate improved axial resolving and localization capabilities, and whole-body C. elegans muscle imaging shows the recovery of structures near the NFP. To demonstrate the feasibility of MoLiS-LFM for in vivo imaging, we applied it to whole-brain imaging in larval zebrafish and achieved cellular-scale volumetric imaging over a 550 × 550 × 200~ μ m 3 volume at 9.06 volumes per second.

candidates.title: Vector Light Field Generation
NIR-II squeezed light-field microscopy enables high-speed volumetric imaging of deep-tissue dynamics in vivo
candidates.abstract: High-speed three-dimensional imaging in scattering biological tissues remains challenging because volumetric microscopy generally requires scanning, whereas snapshot light-field approaches divide limited detector pixels among multiple views. This constraint is particularly severe in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II), where InGaAs cameras have small sensor formats and high detector noise. Here we introduce NIR-II squeezed light-field microscopy (NIR-II SLIM), which optically rotates and compresses multiple perspective views before detection, allowing efficient use of camera pixels while retaining complementary spatial information for three-dimensional reconstruction. NIR-II SLIM acquires up to 600 volumes s-1 with a reconstructed lateral sampling grid of 512 x 512 pixels. We use this method for label-free imaging of cardiac dynamics in pigmented late-larval zebrafish, resolving chamber deformation and millisecond-scale atrioventricular-valve motion, and for NIR-II fluorescence imaging of vascular and lymphatic transport in mice. NIR-II SLIM provides a detector-efficient approach for high-speed volumetric imaging of rapid biological dynamics in scattering tissues.

candidates.title: Scene Complexity-Adaptive 3D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale High-Fidelity Reconstruction and Light Field Visualization
candidates.abstract: We present an end-to-end framework that tightly couples large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstruction with immersive 3D light field rendering and display, enabling efficient reconstruction and high-fidelity 3D visualization. Inspired by human visual perception, we propose an adaptive, scene-complexity-aware 3D Gaussian regulation algorithm driven by an asymmetric safety-valve strategy. By jointly analyzing local texture and disparity, the method preferentially allocates computational resources to perceptually salient regions. In predominantly complex scenes, it prioritizes fidelity, achieving up to a 1.56 dB PSNR improvement. For scenes with significant spatial variation, it reduces training time by 7-52%. The approach can simultaneously improve fidelity by more than 1.0 dB and reduce the primitive count by 7-24%, providing a favorable fidelity-efficiency trade-off compared with CityGS. We also introduce a ray-tracing-based off-axis mapping model that directly maps the Gaussian representation to light field display space, eliminating dense multi-view synthesis and decoupling rendering cost from viewpoint count. Experiments on an 8K, 100-view light field display demonstrate an approximately 4.7× speedup while maintaining high visual fidelity.

candidates.title: Dual-Spectrum Three-Dimensional Light Field Microscopic System Using Deep Learning-Based End-to-End Multimodal Fusion Network
candidates.abstract: We propose a high-precision three-dimensional microscopic display system capable of simultaneous dual-spectral acquisition using visible and short-wave infrared sensors. To achieve accurate, high-fidelity three-dimensional reconstructions, the system integrates a deep learning-based end-to-end multimodal fusion network. This architecture effectively synthesizes data from disparate spectral channels to generate high-precision three-dimensional models of microscopic specimens with enhanced topological detail and contrast.

candidates.title: End-to-end super-resolution computational imaging with super-oscillatory light field
candidates.abstract: Super-oscillatory (SO) imaging provides a promising pathway for far-field, non-invasive, pure-optical super-resolution. Shrinking the central focal spot is a common way used in SO design to pursue finer resolution. However, this inevitably results in huge side-lobes and low central intensity. This results in a severely restricted field of view (FOV) and poor image quality, hindering practical single-shot imaging. Here, we propose an end-to-end joint optimization framework combining the physical SO light field with a backend computational method. Instead of optimizing the isolated SO spot, we directly incorporate the ultimate resolving capability into the optical design loop. Specifically, the physical point spread function is parameterized and optimized by simulating the entire forward imaging and deconvolution process, effectively avoiding the severe noise amplification and reconstruction artifacts that typically plague conventional super-oscillatory field designs, and enhancing the resolution. As a demonstration, our system successfully breaks the diffraction limit, resolving double-hole structures at 0.77 times the diffraction-limited resolution. Furthermore, as our deconvolution model is completely general and assumes no prior knowledge of the object, this scan-free approach is effectively extended to the super-resolution imaging of extended targets, successfully overcoming conventional FOV limitations.

candidates.title: Slim super multi-view virtual reality near-eye display using micro-lens array and dynamically driven point light source array
candidates.abstract: Realizing slim virtual-reality near-eye displays remains challenging due to the large optical path length required by conventional eyepiece optics and the vergence-accommodation conflict (VAC). We present a slim super multi-view (SMV) near-eye display (NED) that combines a micro-lens array (MLA) with a dynamically driven point light source array (PLSA). The MLA forms an intermediate image to reduce the required panel-to-eyepiece distance and simultaneously images the PLSA onto the pupil plane, producing a Maxwellian-view spot that extends depth of focus. By time-multiplexing pupil-plane viewpoints with a synchronized elemental image panel, the proposed system delivers view-dependent disparity within the pupil, thereby providing monocular accommodation cues via dynamically shifting viewpoints. After validating the concept with a benchtop prototype, we further demonstrate an OLED-based PLSA designed for a compact, wearable configuration. By selectively emitting light only at required point-source locations, this system achieves significantly enhanced brightness and contrast.

candidates.title: Proof of realizing arbitrary unitary light transformation based on polarized diffractive optical networks
candidates.abstract: Diffractive optical networks (DONs) enable arbitrary unitary transformations but are typically limited to scalar light fields. This limitation is overcome by introducing polarized diffractive optical networks (PDONs) composed of cascaded birefringent metasurfaces. In this work, we prove that a cascade of birefringent metasurfaces provides sufficient degrees of freedom to synthesize any unitary transformation on the joint polarization and spatial mode space. In addition, the results also indicate that PDONs can realize arbitrary unitary transformations even under non-paraxial conditions, confirming that their operational regime extends beyond the paraxial approximation.

Experimental and numerical investigation of the effect of the spatial coherence of incident light on the Talbot and Lau self-images
candidates.abstract: Using binary gratings as test objects, we quantitatively investigate the formation and visibility of the Talbot and Lau self-images under partially coherent illumination generated by a secondary Gaussian Schell-model source. The spatial coherence of the illuminating field is controlled through continuous variation of the source size, resulting in different fringe distributions in both regimes. Although the spatial coherence length varies according to a Lorentzian function with the source size, the visibility of the Talbot self-images exhibits an approximately Gaussian dependence, decreasing to 0.5 when the coherence length at the grating plane becomes nearly twice the grating pitch. In the Lau regime, the self-images remain sharp and clearly visible over a broad range of low-coherence illumination, as long as the coherence length remains below approximately twice the pitch of the first grating. However, when the coherence length becomes comparable to the grating pitch yet much smaller than the transverse width of the incident light field, the illumination becomes locally coherent over individual grating periods. Consequently, Fresnel diffraction features produced by the gratings appear within the main Lau self-image on the CCD plane, superimpose on the Lau fringes, and degrade their regular structure.
