candidates.title: How light reshapes the mind. An active inference framework for the cognitive and emotional effects of indoor lighting
candidates.abstract: Indoor lighting influences cognition, affect, and behavioral regulation, yet these effects are typically studied as isolated empirical findings rather than as components of a unified computational process. This paper proposes an active inference account of the impact of shared indoor lighting—non-personalized illumination in environments occupied by multiple users such as offices, classrooms, and libraries. The central hypothesis is that lighting acts through three computationally distinct channels, each indexed by a metrologically separable descriptor of the light field rather than by correlated color temperature (CCT): an epistemic channel driven by task-plane photopic illuminance, an affective channel driven by ambient melanopic equivalent daylight illuminance (melanopic EDI; CIE S 026:2018), and a normative channel driven by chromaticity. Because melanopic EDI and chromaticity are dissociable by metamerism, and because the affective input is a whole-field, session-integrated quantity whereas the epistemic input is local and instantaneous, the three channels are separable both in computational role and in physical driver. To formalize and test this hypothesis, the paper develops a proof-of-concept partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) under the active inference framework. The model simulates a cognitive agent performing sustained reading over a 5-h session, receiving observations from two modalities simultaneously: reading performance and eye tracking. Text legibility is a symmetric function of illuminance; the oculomotor signal is asymmetric, degrading rapidly under glare due to pupil constriction, and flat under sub-optimal illuminance. Three factors are crossed in a full factorial design: lighting scenario (warm-dim, moderate, and bright-cool), chronotype (morning, intermediate, and evening), and spatial desk position in a realistically specified room with a simulated photometric field. Six falsifiable predictions are derived from the model structure. These six predictions fall into three tiers by evidential status—structural invariants that verify the implementation (P1, P2, and P6), the critical test of the multi-channel hypothesis (P3, P4), and one exploratory prediction (P5)—and are borne out in simulation at N MC = 20 replicates. The central prediction concerns the spatial ordering of performance under intense cool illumination. Under moderate light, performance follows the legibility gradient: the best-lit desk position produces the best output. Under intense cool light, this ordering completely inverts: the desk position with the best legibility in both channels—receiving only 402 lux at the far corner—produces higher reading speed (71.3 wpm) than the position with near-zero legibility in both channels under 1,200 lux of glare (59.9 wpm). The inversion arises from two concurrent mechanisms: the well-lit agent accurately perceives its deteriorating state and rests strategically, while the glare-blinded agent works blindly through its deterioration but pays a direct mechanical speed penalty. In this condition, strategic rest at the far-corner position yields higher total output than blind persistence under severe glare. This prediction requires the multi-channel architecture and is not expected under models in which lighting acts only through arousal or only through monotonic legibility. Additional predictions include a chronotype-specific risk sign-reversal between scenarios, a position-by-chronotype interaction differing by a factor of two between morning and evening types, and a structural invariance of the intermediate chronotype's EFE risk across all scenarios as a direct consequence of setting its affective tolerance factor to zero. The contribution of the paper is theoretical: it does not provide a calibrated model of human reading performance, but a computational framework that links empirical findings on lighting to an explicit generative architecture with testable, non-trivial signatures. In short, the paper offers a computational theory of light as a modulator of inference, arousal, and behavior, and translates it into concrete experimental predictions.

candidates.title: LFCD-Net: physics-inspired 3D reconstruction architecture for miniature light-field microscopy
candidates.abstract: Abstract Miniature light-field microscopy is a vital tool for high-speed volumetric imaging in freely moving animals, yet its spatial resolution is constrained by the insufficient sampling inherent in simultaneous spatial-angular acquisition. To address this, we propose a physics inspired light-field characteristic driven 3D reconstruction network integrating three core innovations: spatial-angular feature blocks for aliasing suppression, multi-scale feature blocks for structural fidelity, and a physics-inspired adaptive weighting loss to ensure high-quality reconstruction of sparse biological signals. These modules tackle the sampling deficiency to effectively restore spatial resolution. Crucially, we developed the first miniature dual-path imaging system to provide high-quality paired training data. Simulations demonstrate that our method achieves a lateral resolution of 5.69 μ m , representing a 22% improvement over state-of-the-art deep learning methods and significantly outperforming traditional physics-based algorithms. Validations on complex biological structures and physical experiments across a large 500 μ m depth-of-field confirm superior axial stability and reconstruction accuracy, providing a reliable technical pathway for high-resolution in vivo 3D imaging.

candidates.title: Multi-mode neural network for complex phase modulation in light field 3D displays
candidates.abstract: A mode-embedded neural method is developed for complex phase design of a two-dimensional (2D) single-layer liquid crystal (LC) lens array in light-field three-dimensional (3D) displays. Complementary models learn the nonlinear relationships among electrode voltages, simulated optical responses, and experimentally reconstructed depth information. The networks generate multiple candidate voltage distributions with alternative Fresnel phase-reset patterns, allowing phase fidelity, irradiance uniformity, crosstalk, and depth of field to be jointly evaluated. The resulting system achieves favorable performance, characterized by low mean adjacent-view crosstalk and a low irradiance coefficient of variation with a simulation-driven network, and a high depth of field with a measurement-driven network. This approach supports intelligent optimization of tunable LC elements for 2D/3D switchable light field displays and adaptive optical systems.

candidates.title: Doped germanium keeps pace with the light field
Extended-depth-of-field Fourier light-field microscopy based on Bessel beams
candidates.abstract: We report Bessel-beam-based Fourier light-field microscopy (Bessel-FLFM), an extended-depth-of-field (DOF) snapshot volumetric imaging method. By integrating annular pupil modulation into Fourier light-field detection, Bessel-FLFM employs an annular microlens array to generate Bessel-like point spread functions, enabling substantial DOF extension for high-resolution volumetric imaging. We further introduce radiality-analysis-based Richardson–Lucy deconvolution for high-resolution three-dimensional reconstruction. Experiments with fluorescent beads demonstrate a 16 μm DOF, with lateral and axial resolutions of approximately 350 and 500 nm, respectively. High-speed volumetric tracking of freely diffusing beads achieves an imaging rate of 100 Hz. Multicolor imaging of biological samples further validates the applicability of Bessel-FLFM for snapshot volumetric fluorescence imaging at subcellular resolution.

candidates.title: Optical Sedan: A Tailored Light Pattern for Controllable Microsphere Manipulation and Autonomous Screening via Optoelectronic Tweezers
candidates.abstract: Abstract Optoelectronic tweezers have shown great potential in micro/nanoscale precision manipulation, but conventional static light fields are difficult to integrate programmable trajectory control and label-free autonomous sorting, which limits their practical application. To solve this problem, this work proposes a composite light field manipulation strategy named the Optical Sedan for Ag-PS microsphere manipulation based on optically induced positive dielectrophoresis. The Optical Sedan is composed of a central circular trapping region and front-rear guiding segments. Experimental results show that single- and dual-Sedan configurations can stably transport microspheres along square, circular, and hexagonal trajectories with a trajectory error of less than 0.6%, while the three-Sedan configuration can realize complex multi-particle behaviors such as counter-directional orbital motion and synchronized crossing, showing excellent light field reconfigurability. In addition, a unique single-particle exclusivity effect is observed for the first time, which can realize spontaneous particle selection without external control, and its mechanism is related to the coupling of electric field distortion and dipole-dipole repulsion between polarized particles. This study provides a new paradigm for the design and application of OET light fields, and has important guiding significance for microfluidic sorting, microstructure assembly, and precise single-particle manipulation.

candidates.title: Coordinate-Aware Implicit Representation for Low-Light Light Field Image Compression and Enhancement
Semi-physical neural-network-based pre-correction toward achromatic crosstalk-free vector light-field 3D display
candidates.abstract: Vector light-field three-dimensional (3D) displays are emerging glass-free solutions for augmented reality and virtual reality to deliver vivid, immersive visual experiences. However, due to unavoidable errors in the design and device fabrication, the viewing experience has been degraded severely by the crosstalk and chromatism in these systems. We present a deep-learning-based pre-correction method that effectively suppresses the chromatism and crosstalk in 3D display systems via the synergy between physics-informed and data-driven model training. With no extra hardware in the 3D display system, this neural network approach enables the suppression of chromatism and crosstalk by the intelligent adjustment of display content, making this approach versatile for any naked-eye display system. We first developed a semi-physics-driven neural network model in which the associated loss function was optimized based on the crosstalk and chromatism mechanism. Furthermore, we built a prototype of the 3D display to validate the ability of the method to enhance display quality. Experimental results show that the method successfully reduces the average crosstalk and average chromatism by 36.37%±3.44% and 38.68%±4.24%, respectively. Therefore, this software-based pre-correction technique is expected to be synergistically combined with hardware optimization efforts in future developments to achieve high-quality, achromatic, and crosstalk-free light-field 3D displays.

candidates.title: Dual Representation-Based Light Field View Synthesis using Deformable Convolutional and Deep Residual Channel Attention Networks
candidates.venue: IEEE Open Journal of Signal Processing

candidates.title: Effect of orbital angular momentum on multipole light-molecule interaction in Laguerre-Gaussian beams
candidates.abstract: In this work, we evaluate the interaction of circularly polarized Laguerre-Gaussian beams with molecular electric-dipole, magnetic-dipole, and electric-quadrupole transition moments. The twisted-light field is described within the paraxial approximation, while its interaction with molecular transition multipole moments is treated using the multipole expansion. This work assesses the applicability of these approximations to describing the interaction of matter with structured light.

candidates.title: Operando X‐ray Spectroscopy Unveils Light‐Driven Redox Selectivity for Photo‐Assisted Li–S Batteries
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Photo‐assisted lithium‐sulfur batteries (PALSBs) can accelerate the sluggish redox kinetics of sulfur cathodes. However, the introduced light field inevitably complicates interfacial reactions, necessitating in situ evidence under realistic operating conditions. Here, we construct a TiO 2 /FePS 3 (TF) p–n junction bifunctional photoelectrode and employ a multiphysics‐coupled in situ x‐ray spectroscopic technique to elucidate light‐regulated catalysis from the interface into the bulk. Operando low‐energy XPS identifies potential interfacial catalytic sites. High‐energy operando XAFS is, for the first time, applied in PALSBs to track the K‐edge position of catalytic centers throughout cycling. The results show that the reversible dynamic valence evolution synchronizes with the stepwise sulfur redox process, revealing that photogenerated carriers and electrocatalytic electrons act cooperatively to promote polysulfide conversion. DFT calculations corroborate, from thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, that illumination strengthens polysulfide anchoring and lowers the energy barriers of key conversion steps, consistent with the operando spectroscopic observations. Benefiting from this photoelectrochemical co‐regulation, the TF‐based PALSB maintains excellent reversible capacity and cycling stability under high sulfur loading and low electrolyte content. This work establishes a characterization paradigm for the rational design of high‐performance photo‐assisted Li–S cathodes.

candidates.title: A Dual-Domain Enhanced Feature Aggregation Network for Light Field Salient Object Detection
Dynamic Light Field Reconstruction and Digital Twin Surrogate Modeling for Multi-Objective Light Environment Optimization of a Vertical Circulating Rice Seedling Rack
candidates.abstract: Vertical circulating rice seedling racks in cold regions of northeast China face limited natural radiation, uneven light distribution, and high energy demand. This study develops a digital twin optimization framework integrating dynamic light field reconstruction, crop physiological response, surrogate modeling, and multi-objective analysis. A solar position algorithm-based simulator reconstructs the spatiotemporal PPFD distribution along the circulating trajectory and couples it with stage-specific rice seedling light response curves. An XGBoost surrogate model is then used to accelerate parameter evaluation for stage-wise optimization. Preliminary measurements using a plant light analyzer showed limited PPFD deviations from simulation, with a mean deviation of −3.4% and a maximum deviation of +11.4%. The surrogate model achieved a test R2 of 0.9955 and a five-fold cross-validation R2 of 0.9933 ± 0.0024. Under the engineering constraint of CV ≤ 0.10, stage-wise optimization identified max yield, best efficiency, and balanced operating strategies. The balanced strategy predicted a 7.7% increase in YI, a 6.0% reduction in energy use, and a decrease in CV from 0.0353 to 0.0058 relative to the fixed-parameter baseline. SHAP analysis further identified growth stage as the dominant structural factor, while lighting duration and rack speed mainly regulated within-stage performance. This framework provides a quantitative basis for stage-aware light environment optimization and subsequent experimental validation.

candidates.title: State-Aware Dependency Reasoning for Light Field Angular Super-Resolution
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology

candidates.title: Enhancing the imaging performance of single-photon array detection through freeform-surface-based light field modulation
candidates.abstract: To address the bottlenecks of low optical efficiency and uneven illumination inherent to single-photon array LiDAR systems, this paper proposes a joint imaging framework combining freeform light field shaping via an orthogonal bidirectional iterative algorithm and total-variation (TV) regularized image reconstruction. The core optical contribution lies in a freeform lens design strategy based on orthogonal bidirectional iteration, which establishes a precise energy mapping between incident Gaussian beams and uniform lattice light fields matching GM-APD pixel layouts. This refractive reshaping converts raw Gaussian radiation into flat-top spot arrays with homogenized energy distribution. Numerical simulations verify that the proposed freeform modulation achieves an optical energy utilization of 89.1% and a light uniformity of 96.5%, fundamentally resolving the tradeoff between central pixel saturation and peripheral detection blind zones in array receivers. For photon-sparse, noise-contaminated raw echo data, a reconstruction workflow integrating maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and conventional TV regularization is adopted to suppress stochastic noise while preserving sharp object geometric edges. Nighttime field experiments targeting a scene at 22.4 m demonstrate that the mean absolute error (MAE) of depth reconstruction is reduced from 2.2373 m under unoptimized flood illumination to 0.3176 m with our freeform lattice illumination. The presented scheme fulfills the large field-of-view (FOV) requirement of array-based single-photon detection and yields remarkable imaging improvements under constraints of limited laser output power and compact optical packaging. This work delivers a feasible optical route for high-efficiency, long-range single-photon 3D imaging LiDAR.

candidates.title: Light Layers™: from technical lighting to spatial image construction
candidates.abstract: The article is devoted to the transition from technical lighting setup to the spatial construction of a photographic image within the four-layer Light Layers™ framework. The purpose of the study is to substantiate a layered sequence of building image depth, in which light is applied to the space of the scene before it is applied to the subject, and to assess the relative weight of each layer. In the course of the scientific study, general scientific methods of cognition were used, in particular analysis, synthesis, comparison, generalization, systematization and the relative importance index. The results of the study show that the photographic market has reached a state where technical equipment no longer separates one commercial offer from another. Statistical data on the growth of business costs, on the ratio of openings to closures and on the redistribution of face-to-face formats of client interaction across three business models were summarized. It was found that formats connected with showing and handing over a finished image are growing, whereas formats of checking and approval are declining. A three-year projection of the sale of a product during a personal meeting was calculated for the three business models, and it showed that the models diverge from more than a doubling of the volume to virtual stagnation. The technologies of technical light control were systematized, in particular light-shaping attachments, the colour rendering index and the colour quality scale, xenon and halogen sources, the quantitative measurement of light harshness through the proportions of a cast shadow, and multi-frame capture with subsequent assembly of the lighting in an editor. It was shown that all of them describe the source and not the scene. The stages of spatial construction of a two-dimensional image were revealed and combined into a single sequence, from the inventory of elements in the frame to the focal point. It was demonstrated that the same depth cues, namely overlapping planes, tonal separation and aerial perspective, are used both in landscape practice and in light field depth estimation. The author's Light Layers™ framework was substantiated, in which the image is built through four layers: atmosphere, space, shape and face. The layers were ranked by the relative importance index on four criteria, and it was established that the order of execution does not coincide with the order of weight. Space received the highest index, while the conventional technical setup on the subject received the lowest, despite being the easiest to teach. The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of using its conclusions by photographers, studio owners and authors of educational programmes to rebuild the sequence of work with light and the sequence of teaching it.

candidates.title: Spectral niches and vertical organization of marine phototrophs: from light attenuation to photophysiological acclimation
candidates.abstract: Marine phototrophs are vertically structured across the water column and benthic habitats in response to pronounced gradients in light intensity and spectral composition. As light propagates through seawater, selective attenuation progressively modifies the underwater light field, generally favoring blue to blue-green wavelengths in clear waters, while dissolved and particulate matter can shift the available spectrum toward greener conditions. These optical gradients generate distinct spectral niches that influence the distribution and performance of cyanobacteria, phytoplankton, macroalgae, and photosynthetic corals. However, vertical organization cannot be explained by wavelength alone. Pigment composition, chromatic acclimation, photoacclimation, morphology, internal optics, and nutrient availability interact to determine the realized depth distribution of marine phototrophs. This mini-review synthesizes evidence across pelagic, coastal, benthic, and sedimentary environments to examine how spectral quality and irradiance jointly shape vertical ecological organization. Particular attention is given to complementary pigment absorption in macroalgae and cyanobacteria, chromatic acclimation in Synechococcus, photoacclimation within deep chlorophyll maxima, and whole-organism optical adaptations in deep-water corals and seaweeds. Available evidence indicates that spectral specialization is most ecologically consequential under conditions of strong light limitation, whereas nutrient–light trade-offs and morphological adaptations can substantially modify or override simple wavelength-based predictions. Vertical organization should therefore be understood as a dynamic outcome of interactions among underwater optical properties, organismal light-harvesting strategies, and resource availability rather than as a fixed sequence of pigment-defined depth zones. This framework also highlights the potential sensitivity of spectral niches to future changes in ocean optical conditions and variability.

candidates.title: Generation and conversion of vortex light in coherently prepared hydrogen atoms and hydrogen-like ions
candidates.abstract: Vortex light not only offers new insights into a broad range of physical phenomena, but also enables advanced applications across multiple disciplines. In this paper, we propose a theoretical scheme for the generation and conversion of vortex light in a three-level Λ-type system, and demonstrate that the process can be realized in hydrogen atoms and hydrogen-like ions. The validity of the theory is verified through numerical results performed within the three-level structure of hydrogen atoms. In addition, we show that the light fields can undergo nearly lossless propagation under conditions of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT). These results provide a feasible pathway for the generation and conversion of vortex light.

candidates.title: Dynamic laser structured light 3D shape measurement for large depth of field and wide field of view
candidates.abstract: Structured light three-dimensional (3D) measurements reconstruct an object’s surface topography through coded light field projection and modulated reflected light analysis. To overcome the limitations of depth of field (DOF) and defocus-induced fringe degradation in conventional digital projection systems, we propose a dynamic laser interference measurement method with a tunable carrier frequency. A grating-prism interferometric configuration based on the Doppler effect is established to generate coherent fringes, and simultaneous expansion of the DOF and field of view (FOV) is achieved via negative lens beam expansion and translation-based tuning. Featuring tunable parameters, a compact structure, and ease of engineering implementation, this method delivers millimeter-level measurement accuracy within a 1200 mm depth range, with a standard sphere radius error below 1.4 mm. Continuous FOV tuning was realized through negative lens translation, which increased the effective spot area by up to 72.22%. The proposed method shows potential for large-scale industrial inspection and may have applicability in intelligent driving.

candidates.title: Single-shot light-field microscopy captures delivery-dependent dye and autofluorescence patterns in Caenorhabditis elegans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional imaging of live Caenorhabditis elegans commonly relies on sequential z-stack acquisition, which can be slow and susceptible to movement and photobleaching. Here, we used light-field microscopy to capture dye and delivery-dependent fluorescence patterns across intact adult worms in a single exposure per channel. With a 40×/1.20 NA water-immersion objective, each reconstructed dataset contained 121 axial slices spanning 109 µm at 0.91 µm spacing. In a representative adult, nematode signal extended from 40.88 to 85.4 µm, corresponding to approximately 44.5 µm of captured axial depth without sequential z scanning. Three fluorescence channels were acquired with a summed exposure time of 112 ms across a 685 × 1010 µm field of view. FM1-43 labelled intestinal, cuticular and vesicular structures, FM4-64 highlighted ingested bacteria and intestinal compartments, and Nile Red revealed vesicular and broader whole-organism fluorescence. Intrinsic blue and green autofluorescence signals were also resolved. These observations demonstrate rapid single-shot acquisition of whole-organism three-dimensional fluorescence information and show how delivery route influences the spatial distribution of commonly used fluorescent probes in C. elegans . Highlights Light-field microscopy captures whole-worm 3D fluorescence in a single exposure A 109 µm axial range is rendered as 121 slices at 0.91 µm spacing FM1-43, FM4-64 and Nile Red show distinct volumetric staining patterns Delivery route alters fluorescence distribution across intact C. elegans Three-channel volumetric imaging uses a summed exposure time of 112 ms

candidates.title: An Ultra‐Compact Broadband Metalens‐Based Structured Light Analyzer
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT High‐precision real‐time characterization of complex spatiotemporal light fields is crucial for super‐resolution imaging and high‐dimensional information processing. However, existing technologies still face challenges such as limited functionalities, restricted accuracy, and complicated measurement procedures. Here, a broadband metasurface‐based structured light analyzer is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Leveraging a neural network‐driven inverse optimization model, the end‐to‐end inverse design of the metalens is achieved within a continuous geometric parameter space. By enabling comprehensive multi‐parameter detection within a monolithic metasurface architecture across the 450–650 nm range, this design offers an ultra‐compact form factor suitable for direct on‐chip integration with CMOS imaging sensors. Experimental results at 488, 532, and 633 nm reveal full Stokes reconstruction errors below 3%, with a polarization reconstruction accuracy comparable to that of commercial polarimeters. Furthermore, the reconstruction accuracy of the wavefront phase gradient is approximately 3%, supporting real‐time wavefront detection with an incident angle of up to 9°. Finally, the dynamic multi‐parameter capture of vector light fields featuring complex polarization and phase distributions is successfully demonstrated. This work provides an effective strategy for designing compact light‐field detection devices, holding promising potential for applications in structured light detection and joint polarization‐phase imaging.

candidates.title: 6‐1: A Real‐Time Eye Tracking System for Man‐to‐Machine Interaction on Light Field Display
candidates.abstract: The rapid expansion of immersive technologies, particularly with light field display, has led to an increase in demand for natural, intuitive interaction methods. Accurate and continuous eye pose tracking becomes essential in such systems to provide viewpoint‐dependent rendering and optimized display resource allocation. However, current neural‐network‐based eye pose tracking models face latency limitations for multi‐viewer scenarios at a distance. We present a hybrid eye pose tracking system that combines neural detection, optical flow, and Kalman filtering with interpupillary‐distance (IPD) based yaw estimation. Embedded into a light‐field prototype, the system achieves an eye tracking range up to 4.5 m with a 360° coverage, a tracking latency below 10 milliseconds, leading to an end‐to‐end motion‐to‐photon latency below 20 milliseconds, which satisfies the perceptual tolerance requirements for motion disparity.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 61‐3: Implementation of a Light Field Display for Personalized Content in Multi‐Viewer Settings Based on Vector Pixel Scanning Technology
candidates.abstract: Achieving light filed display and been a long‐time dream for mankind. While significant progress has already been achieved, there remains many technical challenged including supporting large field of view (FoV) and balancing spatial and angular resolutions. We present a light field display system based on vector pixel scanning (VPS) technology. The system utilizes micro‐LEDs with mounted lens and gratings, which are assembled into a light pole, realizing spatial multiplexing by projecting micro‐LED pixels on to a display surface. These poles are assembled on to a rotor to create a motion scanning screen, realizing time multiplexing of the pixels. Two prototypes are built following this architecture, a desktop cylindrical display which achieves a spatial bandwidth product (SBP) of 190 million and a panoramic hall system with a SBP of 10 billion. Both systems support a 360‐degree FoV and delivering personalized content to each viewer in multi‐viewer settings.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 62‐3: Portable Light‐Field AR Display for In‐Situ 3D Ultrasound Guidance in Emergency Care
candidates.abstract: Ultrasound (US) imaging can effectively support clinicians in Wilderness First Aid (WFA) in performing timely and accurate injury assessments owing to its real‐time, non‐invasive, and radiation‐free imaging capabilities. However, conventional two‐dimensional (2D) US requires clinicians to mentally reconstruct three‐dimensional (3D) anatomy and frequently shift their gaze between the monitor and the operative field, which places substantial demands on their spatial reasoning skills and disrupts the spatial correspondence between the visualized anatomy and the physical workspace. Although previous studies have explored 3D imaging and augmented reality (AR) to enhance spatial perception, existing systems either rely on head‐mounted displays that are unsuitable for outdoor emergency environments or support only 2D visualization, limiting their practicality in WFA and prehospital settings. To overcome these limitations, we propose a portable AR system for in‐situ 3D US visualization tailored to WFA. The system integrates a glasses‐free light field 3D display with a beam splitter, enabling direct overlay of reconstructed 3D US volumes onto the scanning region without head‐mounted devices. A dedicated calibration method compensates for depth‐related imaging deviations to ensure high‐precision spatial alignment. Real‐time 3D reconstruction is achieved using a wireless handheld US probe with pose estimation that fuses inertial measurements and image‐based structural correlations. Experimental results demonstrate an average pose estimation error of 8.64 mm, a spatial display resolution of 2 mm, a viewing angle of 38.6°, and an in‐situ overlay root‐mean‐square error of 0.72 mm. The proposed system provides a portable, accurate, and user‐friendly solution for in‐situ 3D US guidance in wilderness emergency scenarios.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 36‐2: Crosstalk‐Free Content Generation Method for Light Field 3D Displays
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 28‐1: Novel Light Field Display Technology for Commercialization
candidates.abstract: Several factors are critical to the successful commercialization of 3D products, among which the implementation of high‐resolution 3D video with depth perception is essential for delivering a true‐to‐life visual experience in terms of performance. Furthermore, achieving low 3D crosstalk across the entire screen is crucial for accurate depth perception. In this work, we propose a 3D crosstalk analysis method that compensates for fabrication and mass‐production errors to ensure uniform crosstalk across the display, and an FPGA‐based solution to maintain high‐quality 3D imagery under viewer motion.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 77‐2: High‐resolution Automotive Light‐field Head‐Up Display with Eye‐Tracking
candidates.abstract: A high‐resolution head‐up display for automotive applications has been developed. Light field display technology with eye tracking is employed for extended virtual image distance and 3D augmented perception. A field of view of 15° × 5° and an angular resolution of 76.8 pixels per degree is obtained, with a crosstalk as low as 1.7 %, yielding an broader potential for automotive applications.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 86‐2: Distinguished Student & Invited Paper: Ultra‐Wide‐Field autostereoscopic Floating 3D Display Using Isolated‐MLa and Gradual Radius Lens Design
candidates.abstract: an Isolated Microlens array (i‐MLa) light field architecture incorporating Gradual Radius Lens (GRL) design is proposed for realizing an ultra‐wide‐field autostereoscopic floating 3D display in a compact form factor. The system integrates two key techniques: extended coding pitch combined with directional mesh (DM) for substantial crosstalk suppression, and a Gradual Radius Lens (GRL) array with radially varying microlens curvature to enhance image quality at large viewing angles, thereby enabling an ultra‐wide‐field light field system. Optical simulations demonstrate that the fully integrated design achieves a continuous viewing angle of 40° (±20°) at a viewing distance of 500 mm—more than fivefold improvement over conventional light field displays—while preserving image fidelity with minimal degradation across the entire field of view. This work establishes the proposed i‐MLa architecture with integrated Gradual Radius Lens (GRL) as a highly effective solution for realizing ultra‐wide‐field, multi‐user autostereoscopic floating 3D displays while maintaining a compact system thickness
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 86‐4: Invited Paper: Towards High‐Resolution Multi‐Projection Light‐Field Displays with Wide Field of View
candidates.abstract: Traditional multi‐projection light‐field displays require large numbers of projectors, resulting in a bulky form factor and complex system integration. We propose a multi‐projection light field display that replaces conventional projectors with high‐resolution LCD panels, a projection lens array, a directional diffuser, and a convergent backlight module. A Fresnel lens integrated into the backlight module ensures accurate alignment of projected images on the directional diffuser, significantly enhancing both image quality and system compactness. We developed a prototype that delivers clear, continuously varying 3D imagery with a horizontal field of view of approximately 68°.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: 117‐3: Invited Paper: Wide‐viewing Multi‐Projection Light Field Display using Holographic Directional Diffuser
candidates.abstract: We propose a projection‐type light field display that integrates multiple laser beam scanning projectors, a lenticular lens array, and a horizontal directional diffuser. By using oblique projection, the system expands the viewing angle and increases angular density, and a Zernike‐based pre‐warping algorithm corrects off‐axis distortion to achieve stable and precise multiview reconstruction.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: P‐127: Invited Poster: A High‐Resolution Light Field 3D Display Based on Asymmetrical Compound Lenticular Lens Array
candidates.abstract: A high‐resolution light field 3D display based on an asymmetrical compound lenticular lens array is proposed. The asymmetrical compound lenticular lens array is formed by embossing two layers of lenticular lens arrays with different parameters on both sides of a substrate. This configuration enables precise modulation of subpixel light rays to reconstruct voxels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed light field 3D display significantly improves the resolution of 3D images.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: P‐204: Research Progress and Prospects of High‐efficiency Light Extraction Technology for OLED Displays
candidates.abstract: With the development of display technologies towards high performance, low power consumption, and multi‐form factors, Organic Light‐Emitting Diode (OLED) display technology, as one of the mainstream display solutions, has seen its high‐efficiency light extraction technology become a focus of industry attention. This paper systematically reviews the principles, development status, advantages, and challenges of two high‐efficiency light extraction technologies in the OLED field: COE (Color Filter on Encapsulation) and MLA (Micro Lens Array). It focuses on analyzing the technical pathway of COE technology using a single panel to replace the circular polarizer and the mechanism of MLA technology for improving light efficiency through microstructure design. Meanwhile, the potential for combined application of these two technologies and future development directions are discussed, providing a reference for a comprehensive understanding of high‐efficiency light extraction technologies for OLEDs.
candidates.venue: SID Symposium Digest of Technical Papers

candidates.title: Performance characterization framework for light field 3D display
candidates.abstract: Abstract Light field 3D displays are widely considered the optimal pathway for immersive visualization to bridge the physical and digital spaces within the metaverse. However, the lack of a unified theoretical foundation leaves hardware design reliant on empirical heuristics, restricting the deterministic development of light field 3D displays. Here, a performance characterization framework is established by introducing ray-phase space to mathematically analyze light field propagation. With regard to viewing angle, the formation mechanism and distributions of correct and crosstalk rays are characterized, enabling the definition of the complete crosstalk-free viewing zone. Regarding depth and resolution, the propagation induced expansion of light field units is analyzed, leading to a depth-dependent spatial resolution model. Following these definitions, the intrinsic constraints among performance metrics are analyzed within typical parameter ranges. This analysis yields a space-bandwidth-product-based feasible domain, providing a deterministic guideline for initial hardware parameter selection. To validate the proposed framework, a 31.5-inch 8 K light field 3D display prototype utilizing a crossed lenticular lens array was constructed. Experimental results demonstrate good agreement with the analytical model. The measured viewing angle closely matches the analytical limits, and the resolution degradation follows the theoretical prediction, with a coefficient of determination of R 2 = 0.8561 for experimental measurements. These results indicate that the proposed framework can support performance characterization and initial hardware parameter selection for light field 3D display systems.

candidates.title: Light field detection in the age of artificial intelligence
Joint Mask–Dictionary Optimization for Computational Light Field Imaging
candidates.abstract: Compressive light field (CLF) imaging relies on the interplay between sensing and sparse representation, where the coherence between the measurement matrix and the reconstruction dictionary fundamentally determines reconstruction performance. Existing approaches generally optimize either the sensing mask or the reconstruction dictionary separately, leading to limited compatibility between acquisition and reconstruction. To address this issue, this paper proposes a mutual coherence-driven joint optimization framework for computational light field imaging. Specifically, an optimized sensing mask is first designed by minimizing its mutual coherence with a predefined dictionary, producing a measurement matrix better suited for compressive acquisition. A dictionary optimization model is then developed for fixed-mask imaging by jointly considering reconstruction fidelity and measurement consistency under a mutual coherence constraint. The resulting alternating optimization framework effectively improves the compatibility between the sensing process and sparse representation while preserving the practical imaging configuration. Unlike generic sensing-matrix design, the proposed formulations explicitly account for the repeated and spatially shifted mask structure induced by CLF image formation. Experiments on five Stanford light field scenes at sampling ratios of 1/4 and 1/9 show that the optimized mask improves the mean PSNR over the uniform-random mask by 1.21 dB and 2.21 dB, respectively, while the optimized dictionary improves the mean PSNR over K-SVD by 0.70 dB and 0.83 dB, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of adapting either the coded mask or the reconstruction dictionary to the CLF measurement model.

candidates.title: Spatiotemporal all-optical diffractive neural networks empowered by spatiotemporal light field manipulation
candidates.abstract: Abstract All-optical neural networks (AONNs) offer significant potential for feature detection and pattern recognition by leveraging light-speed processing, high parallelism, and low energy consumption. However, traditional AONNs are limited to spatial light intensity distributions for both inputs and outputs, restricting network learning to the spatial-only dimension. To overcome this, we propose a novel spatiotemporal AONN architecture that integrates the time dimension with the spatial domain, enabling simultaneous modulation of light field information across both time and space. In this configuration, the output spatiotemporal light field is spatially filtered, and its temporal signals are detected using a single-pixel detector. This approach integrates the temporal dimension as a core computational resource into the network, driving a paradigm shift in AONNs from “imaging detection” to “temporal analysis”, effectively overcoming the speed bottleneck caused by the bandwidth limitations of traditional 2D array detectors. Moreover, experimental studies demonstrate that the system can accelerate the processing of real-world spatiotemporal lidar signals, facilitating the real-time reconstruction of multi-target moving scenes. Our innovative spatiotemporal AONN design offers enhanced flexibility, faster processing speeds, and superior performance, paving the way for more efficient and effective optical signal processing and computing applications.

candidates.title: Cross-Domain Mesh–Progressive Fusion for Light Field Reconstruction
candidates.abstract: Light field angular super-resolution (LFASR) seeks to recover missing viewpoints from sparsely captured angular samples, while preserving the underlying scene structure across views. This task is complicated by disparity-induced variations, incomplete visibility near occlusion boundaries, and view-dependent appearance changes caused by reflective surfaces. In this work, we propose a Cross-Domain EPI–Spatial–Angular (X-ESA) framework that combines EPI-based geometric modeling with complementary spatial and angular feature extraction. A CSWin-based EPI transformer captures long-range, slope-aligned dependencies, while dedicated convolutional branches refine spatial details and cross-view relationships. These features are integrated through a mesh–progressive fusion strategy, followed by channel attention and spatial residual refinement. Extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive reconstruction performance compared with state-of-the-art LFASR approaches.

candidates.title: Self-supervised denoising of light field microscopy for high-dimensional neural imaging
candidates.venue: Fourth Asia Conference on Advances in Image Processing (AAIP 2026)

candidates.title: Four-dimensional Gaussian adaptive tomography for aberration-corrected, time-lapse 3D imaging using Fourier light-field microscopy
candidates.abstract: Abstract Four-dimensional (4D) microscopy imaging of biological dynamics demands both high-speed volumetric acquisition and high-fidelity reconstruction. While Fourier light-field microscopy (FLFM) enables snapshot 3D imaging, it remains susceptible to optical non-idealities and system-model mismatches, as well as inter-frame inconsistencies in time-lapse reconstruction. Here, we introduce 4D Gaussian adaptive tomography (4DGAT), a physics-informed, two-stage framework coupling a self-calibrating forward model, termed the Joint Pupil-Geometry Model (JPGM), with a temporally deformable 3D Gaussian representation. The static stage employs a reference light-field measurement to jointly optimize a canonical 3D Gaussian scene and JPGM parameters describing pupil aberrations and per-lenslet view geometry. With JPGM fixed, the dynamic stage learns a continuous HexPlane deformation field to map the canonical scene over time, ensuring temporal consistency. To facilitate multiscale biological observations, we further develop a versatile FLFM system supporting multiple objective lenses without optical hardware reconfiguration. Simulations confirm robustness against optical aberrations and per-lenslet shifts. Experimentally, 4DGAT resolves mitochondrial network remodeling in live H9c2 cells with improved tubular continuity and axial definition. In beating zebrafish hearts, it enables artifact-suppressed, chamber-resolved 4D imaging for quantitative analysis of cardiac dynamics and surface-mesh-based mapping of regional deformation. In dense three-color macrophage populations, 4DGAT simultaneously reconstructs and tracks hundreds of cells for volumetric phenotyping and magnetic-mobility analysis validated against flow cytometry. By delivering aberration-corrected, temporally consistent 4D reconstruction and quantitative analysis across subcellular, organ, and single-cell scales, 4DGAT advances FLFM from snapshot volumetric imaging toward multiscale interrogation of biological dynamics across subcellular remodeling, organ-level mechanics, and single-cell functional phenotypes.

candidates.title: Minimalist single-atom geometric metasurface for far-field amplitude and polarization manipulation
candidates.abstract: Metasurfaces offer a compact platform for subwavelength control of multidimensional optical fields, making them promising for high-fidelity vectorial light-field reconstruction. Existing approaches typically address this requirement by introducing additional degrees of freedom, either through nanostructures of varying dimensions or through supercell-based multiplexing. However, using nanostructures with different dimensions can increase fabrication complexity, while supercell-based implementations may introduce unwanted diffraction orders. Here, we present a single-atom geometric metasurface for independent far-field control of amplitude and polarization. The modulation is realized with a modified Gerchberg–Saxton algorithm that optimizes amplitude and polarization using a phase-only hologram. By exploiting the centrosymmetric geometric phase response, the left- and right-handed circularly polarized components are independently encoded and coherently superposed in a selected region, enabling vectorial light fields with arbitrary intensity and polarization distributions. This compact strategy provides a general route toward polarization-encoded encryption, structured light beam generation, and optical data storage.

candidates.title: Multi-plane light conversion-based optical inverse scattering for image recovery in multimode fiber transmission
candidates.abstract: Abstract Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer promising prospects in applications such as medical endoscopic imaging owing to their compact footprints. However, modal coupling and scattering effects during propagation severely constrain their practical deployment. Although existing approaches—such as electronic deep learning and diffractive deep neural networks—partially address this issue, they rely heavily on electronic computation or static 3D-printed diffractive layers, suffering from high hardware dependency and limited operational flexibility. In contrast, multi-plane light conversion (MPLC) technology efficiently transforms spatial light fields in free space and enables dynamic mode control via spatial light modulators, providing an effective approach to optical inverse problems with high adaptability across diverse application scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose an MPLC-based image restoration method for MMF transmission, where cascaded phase masks are constructed via a wavefront matching technique to achieve direct, high-efficiency all-optical inverse scattering for image recovery. During numerical modeling, an adaptive weight adjustment mechanism for mask updating and a mean structural similarity index (MSSIM) threshold module were integrated to enhance system stability and recovery performance. Furthermore, phase mask noise, propagation channel noise, and photodetector noise were incorporated into the image recovery process to realistically reflect external perturbations during transmission. Simulation results indicate that for handwritten digit images from the test set transmitted through a 1 m-long MMF, the restored light field achieves a low insertion loss down to 1 dB, an MSSIM of 0.72 ± 0.04 , and a reduced SSIM standard deviation of 0.044. The proposed architecture provides an effective all-optical solution for MMF image recovery, holding significant potential for applications such as medical endoscopic imaging.

candidates.title: Multi-view consistent 3D light-field-driven display method for dynamic digital humans
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a multi-view consistent digital human reconstruction framework for three-dimensional (3D) light-field displays. Existing digital human reconstruction methods often emphasize single-view rendering quality, which may lead to geometric drift and cross-view inconsistency under dense-view display conditions. To address these limitations, an explicit facial mesh anchors Gaussian primitives through bounded residual offsets to improve geometric stability, while a spatial-angular attention network is embedded into 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) to jointly model fine-grained spatial details and view-dependent appearance. Furthermore, RGB, perceptual, and SSIM errors between rasterized images and ground-truth observations at calibrated camera viewpoints are back-propagated through the differentiable rasterizer to optimize Gaussian parameters; the physical light-field display is used for downstream validation. On temporally held-out test splits of three self-captured avatars, the proposed method achieves macro-average PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID values of 27.70 dB, 0.880, 0.097, and 18.71, respectively. The full model further achieves a warped cross-view error (WCVE) of 0.0213, compared with 0.0387 for the baseline. The generated digital humans exhibit improved geometric stability and view-dependent appearance consistency, enabling coherent 3D visualization on a physical light-field display.

candidates.title: Fused visible and active light-based fingerprint recognition for lunar obstacle detection
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes a visible light and active light fusion obstacle fingerprinting technique for the obstacle recognition challenge under the complex light environment on the lunar surface. The method obtains the lunar surface terrain data through visible light images and combines the active light field of view compensation information of the lunar rover to complete the path recognition of the moon. Obstacle features are extracted using Otsu algorithm, morphological processing, and a multispectral fingerprinting model is introduced to achieve high-precision obstacle classification. The experiments are conducted in a simulated lunar surface scene, and the results show that the method achieves 95.7% obstacle recognition accuracy under low-light conditions, and the misclassification rate is reduced to 4.3%, which significantly improves the perception reliability of the unmanned rover in extreme environments. This study provides a new solution that can be referred to for autonomous obstacle avoidance systems for deep space exploration.

candidates.title: Design and implementation of an air-floating 3D light field display system with natural gesture interaction
candidates.abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of low light utilization efficiency, severe ghost image interference and inadequate natural interaction in traditional retro-reflective air-floating 3D display systems, this paper proposes a high-performance air-floating 3D light field display system integrated with natural gesture interaction. A critical incident angle model of straylight in micro-corner prism units is established to optimize structural parameters and suppress stray light. A polarized optical system based on a polarizing beam splitter (PBS) and a quarter-wave plate (QWP) is designed, which improves light utilization efficiency from 22.5% to over 90%. Leap Motion technology is integrated to build a spatial coordinate mapping model between the gesture recognition area and the floating display area, and three natural interactive gestures(translation, rotation, scaling) are implemented for real-time touchless interaction. A ghost image suppression strategy by adjusting the tilt angle of the retro-reflective film is proposed to eliminate ghost interference without additional optical elements or light efficiency loss. A prototype is developed, achieving an air-floating distance of 150–200 mm, a field of view of 30°–35°, a gesture recognition accuracy of 0.01 mm and an interaction response time of less than 10 ms. This research provides a new technical approach for air-floating 3D light field display and exhibits important theoretical and engineering value in virtual reality, augmented reality and human-computer interaction.

candidates.title: Independent Amplitude‐Phase Control in Liquid Crystal for Near‐Field Anti‐Counterfeiting and Far‐Field Holographic Encryption
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal (LC) optical devices provide a promising platform for optical encryption and anti‐counterfeiting applications. However, conventional design paradigms for LC light‐field modulation often involve coupled amplitude and phase responses, limiting design flexibility and information multiplexing capability. Here, we propose a macro‐pixel LC design strategy that enables complex‐amplitude modulation through the coherent superposition of light fields from paired sub‐pixels. In each macro‐pixel, the difference and sum of the LC molecular orientation angles between adjacent sub‐pixel units are tailored to independently control and encode the amplitude and phase of the light field, respectively. This design produces polarization‐insensitive near‐field amplitude modulation, while its spin‐dependent phase response enables polarization‐selective far‐field holographic reconstruction. By further exploiting the distance selectivity of light propagation, we construct an optical security device that encodes a directly observable near‐field anti‐counterfeiting pattern and multiple hidden far‐field holographic images into the same architecture. The hidden holographic information is selectively reconstructed only when the incident polarization state and propagation distance match the predefined physical readout conditions. This macro‐pixel strategy expands the light‐field modulation capability of LC devices and offers a compact route toward near‐ and far‐field information multiplexing, multichannel holographic encryption, and multilevel optical authentication.

candidates.title: Rapid volumetric reconstruction and tracking for Fourier light-field microscopy enables real-time calcium imaging in freely behaving Hydra.
candidates.abstract: Fourier light field microscopy (FLFM) enables high-speed volumetric imaging by encoding multiple angular perspectives of a three-dimensional sample onto a single image. For this reason, FLFM is well-suited to sparse and rapidly evolving biological systems. To aid in the adoption of FLFM, we present OpenFLR, an open-source software framework for real-time volumetric reconstruction, three-dimensional particle tracking, and calcium image processing using FLFM. OpenFLR reconstruction is distributed as four interchangeable interfaces: a Python library, a command-line script, an interactive web application, and an ImageJ/micromanager plugin, so that the pipeline is accessible to both developers and bench biologists. Building on established Richardson-Lucy deconvolution, we use a hybrid experimental-computational PSF calibration strategy and a triangulation approach to tracking to extract particle positions in 3D directly from raw light field frames, bypassing reconstruction. We validate the complete pipeline on GCaMP6s recordings of freely behaving Hydra vulgaris, tracking sparse populations of neurons as they undergo large three-dimensional displacements.

candidates.title: Pointlike Material Accumulation and Displacement in Azopolymer Thin Films Driven by Spatial Light Modulation
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT We report a method for precise surface structuring of azobenzene‐functionalized polymer films using a spatial light modulator (SLM) to generate tailored vectorial light fields with controlled polarization distributions. This approach enables the direct inscription of localized surface features such as single and multiple high‐aspect‐ratio spikes and deep holes of micrometer size, harnessing the light‐induced reorientation of azobenzene molecules within the polymer matrix. The vectorial light field used to create these topographies resembles the distribution of the local optical axis of liquid crystals employed in the fabrication of q‐plates. The resulting molecular realignment induces anisotropic internal stresses, leading to viscoplastic deformation and the formation of complex, programmable surface structures far beyond the periodic patterns achievable with conventional two‐beam interference lithography. Our method confirms the Viscoplastic PhotoAlignment (VPA) model under localized excitation, while also offering a practical and reversible tool for high‐resolution surface patterning. These results establish a platform for the fabrication of programmable materials with potential applications in adaptive optics, microfluidic systems, and surface‐based sensing.

candidates.title: PCA-Based Spatial Light-Field modeling for Anomaly Detection and Compensation in Work-Plane Illuminance Sensor Arrays
candidates.abstract: Development of sensing, networking, and LED dimming have shifted lighting control toward sensor-driven, closed-loop and adaptive operation. In such systems, work-plane sensors provide precise local feedback but are vulnerable to occlusion by documents, equipment, or occupants, which can distort measurements and trigger inappropriate dimming responses. To address this problem, this study proposes a PCA-based spatial-consistency framework for reliable work-plane illuminance sensing array. By analyzing the spatial structure of the daylight residual field, the framework detects and classify anomalies and applies either sensor reconstruction or model updating. Its performance is evaluated through simulation experiments and field validation. Simulation results showed that the non-occluded daylight residual field retained a predominantly low-dimensional structure, supporting healthy PCA modeling. The proposed method reliably detected and localized single-sensor deviations from approximately 15%, corresponding to a median absolute illuminance change of about 8.55 lx in the present experiment, and distinguished localized sensor occlusion from regional light-field disturbances with a balanced accuracy of 87.7%. During 120 min of continuous occlusion, PCA reconstruction maintained a mean absolute error of approximately 9.34 lx. Field validation further confirmed the integrated closed-loop operation of anomaly detection, sensor reconstruction, and healthy PCA model updating under physical sensor occlusion and regional light-field disturbances. Overall, the proposed framework improves the reliability of work-plane illuminance sensing without additional sensing hardware and supports fault-tolerant lighting control.

candidates.title: Single‐Pulse Femtosecond Laser 3D Multi‐Foci Light‐Field Engineering via Multi‐Layer Noise Threshold Filtering
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional processing is a key trend in micro/nano manufacturing, with widespread applications in photonics, manufacturing, and optical storage. However, simultaneously achieving high fabrication resolution, throughput, and quality for three‐dimensional structures remains challenging. Here, we propose a three‐dimensional multi‐foci light‐field shaping and high‐throughput micro/nano manufacturing method based on a single pulse. This method combines a multi‐layer noise threshold filtering algorithm with a multi‐layer over‐sampling algorithm to generate a three‐dimensional multi‐foci light field with up to 5,400 laser foci across six layers using a dual‐spatial‐light‐modulator parallel system. In processing experiments, a representative single‐spatial‐light‐modulator light field contains 1,200 laser foci per pulse. Under the dual‐spatial‐light‐modulator parallel system, this configuration corresponds to 2,400 processing points per incident pulse, enabling a demonstrated processing throughput of 24 000 000 processing points s −1 . In addition, the method achieves an isolated smallest feature of approximately 50 nm and demonstrates high manufacturing flexibility and broad material compatibility across inorganic, organic, and hydrogel materials. This strategy provides a precise, scalable, and efficient route for high‐quality three‐dimensional micro/nano manufacturing.

candidates.title: Advances in Versatile Light Field Manipulation with On-Chip Metasurfaces
candidates.abstract: The relentless pursuit of higher information density and processing speed has driven photonic chips toward miniaturization, high performance, and multifunctional integration. Metasurfaces, composed of subwavelength artificial meta-atoms, have emerged as a revolutionary platform for manipulating light fields at the nanoscale, offering unprecedented control over amplitude, phase and polarization, as well as enabling frequency conversion through nonlinear processes. When seamlessly integrated with on-chip optical waveguides, metasurfaces provide a compelling solution for bridging guided waves and free-space waves, enabling compact, high-performance photonic devices with versatile light-manipulation capabilities. This review systematically surveys recent advances in on-chip metasurfaces for multifunctional light field manipulation, with a focus on guided-wave radiation control. We first elucidate the fundamental phase modulation mechanisms that collectively constitute a versatile toolbox for tailoring light fields at subwavelength scales. We then examine the three core application scenarios that define the operational framework of metasurface-integrated photonic systems: free-space-to-chip coupling, in-plane guided-wave manipulation, and guided-wave-to-free-space radiation. For each scenario, we highlight representative device architectures and their performance characteristics, tracing the evolution from single-mechanism modulation to multidimensional multiplexing and dynamic reconfigurability. We conclude by discussing remaining challenges including efficiency, dynamic tunability, and scalable fabrication, and outline future directions such as intelligent inverse design, on-chip quantum metasurfaces, and optical computing.

candidates.title: MetaLFM: Metalens-array-enabled High-Density Optical Sampling for High-Resolution Volumetric Bioimaging by Light Field Microscopy
candidates.abstract: Abstract Light field microscopy enables snapshot volumetric imaging by simultaneously capturing spatial and angular information. However, its imaging performance is fundamentally governed by the sampling geometry of the microlens array. Increasing the sampling density through reduced lens pitch is desirable for improving spatial resolution yet implementing small-pitch refractive microlens arrays while maintaining the focal length and f-number required for LFM becomes increasingly challenging because of geometric fabrication constraints. Here, we present MetaLFM, a metalens-array-enabled high-density optical sampling architecture for high-resolution volumetric bioimaging. A large-area TiO 2 metalens array with a 75-µm pitch and a designed focal length of 1430 µm was engineered to provide reduced-pitch sampling while maintaining the f-number matching condition required for light field acquisition. Experimental characterization demonstrated consistent focusing performance across the fabricated array and confirmed a stable operating condition for spatial–angular light-field sampling. Compared with conventional LFM using a 100-µm-pitch refractive microlens array, MetaLFM reduced the reconstructed lateral and axial full width at half maximum by up to 44% and 39%, respectively, across the evaluated imaging depth, while reducing grid-like reconstruction artifacts near the native image plane. Volumetric imaging of mouse spinal cord tissue and human intestinal organoids showed improved structural delineation and reconstruction fidelity, while 25 Hz calcium imaging of primary cortical neurons demonstrated applicability to dynamic bioimaging. These results expand the resolution–depth capabilities of light field microscopy for high-resolution volumetric bioimaging.

candidates.title: Enhanced epsilon-near-zero metamaterials for efficient light field control
candidates.abstract: Enhanced epsilon-near-zero (eENZ) metamaterials based on resonant ENZ–dielectric multilayer stacks provide a powerful platform for controlling the properties of light. Unlike effective-medium ENZ structures, these stratified metamaterials exploit Fabry–Pérot resonances, guided modes, and plasmonic excitations to strongly enhance transmission, reflection, or absorption near the ENZ wavelength while mitigating intrinsic material losses. The design and principles of eENZ structures are reviewed together with their theoretical capabilities. Previously reported fabrication of eENZ structures from indium tin oxide and titanium dioxide thin films is discussed and their experimentally demonstrated capabilities are assessed. The eENZ metamaterial may be positioned as a versatile building block for novel active and reconfigurable photonic systems.

candidates.title: Preliminary development of a DMD–metalens light-field system through automated metalens synthesis
candidates.abstract: A preliminary workflow for metalens design from prescribed ray bundles is investigated for light-field generation near a digital micromirror device (DMD). From the target ray geometry, phase maps and corresponding pillar layouts are generated automatically. The approach is demonstrated through the design and simulation of a metalens that focuses an obliquely incident beam onto selected positions on the DMD mirror.

candidates.title: Taming light topology with advanced metasurfaces
candidates.abstract: Optical beams exhibiting skyrmionic textures of the Stokes vector have recently emerged as a promising platform due to their intrinsic topological protection and rich polarization structure. However, compact and versatile approaches for their generation and control are still lacking. Here, we report dualfunctional dielectric metasurfaces enabling the tailored generation and reconfigurable control of skyrmionic light fields during propagation. By exploiting anisotropic metaatoms, the designed metaoptics allow simultaneous and asymmetric manipulation of orthogonal polarization states within a single element, yielding full Poincaré beams with skyrmionic topology in 2D and 3D (optical hopfions). Advanced phase engineering enable a rich variety of dynamical effects during propagation as polarization beating and topology reconfigurability. This work demonstrates a versatile framework for the custom generation and manipulation of topological beams, opening new opportunities for robust photonic functionalities in emerging technologies based on topological invariants.

candidates.title: Wavefront diagnosis of a Fourier light-field microscope using aberrations in Zemax
candidates.abstract: Fourier light-field microscopy (FLFM) enables single-shot 3D imaging by placing a microlens array at the Fourier plane conjugate to the objective's aperture stop, yielding a spatially invariant 3D point-spread function and artifact-free reconstruction. This performance depends critically on a near-diffraction-limited wavefront reaching the pupil. We present a full digital replication and diagnostic study of a high-NA (1.1, water-immersion) FLFM setup in Zemax OpticStudio, built to reproduce our physical laboratory system from the laser source through the illumination relay onto the objective back focal plane. As the manufacturer discloses no model of the commercial objective, we designed an equivalent 1.1-NA water-immersion objective from scratch, matching its key specifications, to serve as a controlled reference. The system still failed to collimate, proving the four-lens illumination relay — not the objective — as the source of degradation. Because the commercial tube lens is provided only as a black-box element, standard Seidel analysis is inapplicable; we therefore extracted Zernike Standard Coefficients to quantify the higher-order phase errors across the pupil. This work establishes a hardware-level verification workflow for FLFM and provides the corrected wavefront baseline required for subsequent Fourier-plane microlens-array design.

candidates.title: Research on the light-field characteristics of fan-shaped partitioned liquid crystal microlenses
candidates.abstract: An electrically controlled liquid crystal (LC) microlens array based on fan-shaped partitioned planar pattern electrodes is reported in this paper, which can achieve efficient light wave modulation in a block-wise manner. By jointly driving and controlling the voltages of array electrodes in different regions within the same substrate of LC microlenses, corresponding adjustable focal point-like light spots can be formed. This method will provide inspiration for the continuous development and design of LC optical components, promoting the development of applications such as light-field imaging, wavefront detection/correction, and imaging enhancement systems.

candidates.title: Nanophotonic manipulation of structured light: From free-space to polaritonics
candidates.abstract: Structured light underpins a wide range of modern photonic technologies. In this talk, I will present several nanophotonic platforms for the generation, manipulation, and detection of structured light fields, including disordered mosaic metasurfaces, complex‑amplitude metasurface holograms, a multifunctional metasurface integrated with quantum emitters, optical metafibres, and on‑chip polaritonic surfaces capable of generating subwavelength vortex fields.

Precision measurement of high-aspect-ratio micro-hole aperture based on far-field diffraction FWHM analysis of Gaussian beams
candidates.abstract: To address the challenge of accurately measuring the aperture of high-aspect-ratio thick pinholes used in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) diagnostics, a non-contact aperture inversion method based on the far-field diffraction full width at half maximum (FWHM) of a Gaussian beam is proposed. Addressing the limitations of the traditional thin-aperture Airy model—which neglects waveguide confinement, edge truncation, and inner-wall scattering—a hybrid light-field reconstruction (HLFR) model is established and propagated using angular spectrum theory. Comparative analysis shows that the main spot FWHM exhibits superior robustness against wavefront non-uniformity and non-ideal scattering compared to conventional Airy pattern features. By applying a dual-parameter adaptive correction combining aperture and hole length across 25 simulated samples, the relative FWHM inversion error is significantly reduced from 8.72% to within 1.20%. Experimental validation on four physical thick pinholes demonstrates strong consistency across propagation distances, with a blind-test deviation of approximately 0.5%. This work provides a highly accurate and robust non-contact technical approach for the geometric inspection of large aspect ratio microstructures.

candidates.title: Fast continuous tissue oxygenation visualization for colorectal surgery using hyperspectral light-field imaging
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reliable bowel perfusion assessment remains difficult because intraoperative judgement is largely subjective and many hyperspectral imaging workflows are intermittent. We present a workflow-compatible approach for fast continuous tissue oxygenation visualization during colorectal surgery using hyperspectral light-field imaging. The method combines reflectance reconstruction with a computationally efficient spectral correlation to generate color-coded oxygenation overlays during the extracorporal surgical phase. In a two-case pilot study, the oxygenation transition zones corresponded well with surgeon-defined transection regions and supported temporal visualization of progressive devascularization. Two hyperspectral light-field cameras were evaluated in parallel. Total processing times of 161.5 ms and 397.2 ms enabled continuous image guidance, while the camera comparison remained secondary to the translational objective. The results indicate that hyperspectral light-field imaging is a promising platform for intraoperative perfusion guidance in colorectal surgery.

candidates.title: A low-latency and high-speed 3D estimation with the light field microscopy
candidates.abstract: Three dimensional (3D) observation of living microorganisms and cells under a microscope has attracted considerable attention. In particular, when automated control of microscopic system is necessary, obtaining three-dimensional information with low latency is particularly crucial. This is because the performance of such automated control systems depends on the total latency included in the feedback loop. Therefore, in the paper, we proposed a low-latency and high-speed 3D estimation based on the light field microscopy (LFM) applied to high-speed optimal focal plane determination. A developed prototype system demonstrated a total latency of 2.58 ± 0.54 ms. This approach is also expected to be applied to future auto-focusing platforms.
